beats.text: Your money doesn't actually move when you pay by UPI.
Not in those two seconds, anyway.
You scan a QR code at a tea stall. Your app sends the request to its bank.
That bank passes it to NPCI, the switchboard that sits between every UPI bank in India.
NPCI looks up the UPI ID, like name@bank, and finds which bank account it points to.
Then it asks your bank one question: does this person have the money?
Your bank checks your PIN and your balance, and takes the amount out of your account.
NPCI tells the shopkeeper's bank, which adds it to their account. Ding. Paid.
The banks settle the real money between themselves later, in batches.
And the scale is wild: in August twenty twenty-six, UPI handled twenty-four point five billion payments in a single month.
